jobs.scene: An archaeological object study of the completed composite hand spear, without a construction cutaway or measured proportions.
jobs.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: Humanity Handbook manual plate. Image 1 supplies graphic style ONLY: navy ink, restrained pastel watercolour, warm ivory paper, sparse large serif uppercase title, thin leader lines. Do not copy its digging stick. General design study, no exact measurements, load rating, universal recipe or performance claim.

Image 2 supplies ONLY the small stout leaf-shaped stone insert geometry, not an unmounted status. Title exactly "STONE-POINTED SPEAR". One ordinary straight OAK HAND SPEAR, long shaft, modest grey stone tip finger-length in real use, shown across landscape page. Point is short stout leaf-shaped with broad plain base, no barbs or tang, no metal. Base sits in shallow controlled terminal cleft with a SUPPORTED STOP, shaft wood on BOTH sides, axis aligned. Dense simple plant-cord turns retain the mounting zone BEHIND sharp forward edges, with a separate retaining band just below the terminal cleft limiting split propagation. Do not wrap cord over the pointed cutting tip. No glue, broad decorative ribbons or spearhead the size of a shield.
Enlarged simple CUTAWAY inset clearly shows broad base seated against sound wood rather than floating loose in a hollow; a partial near-side wood section can be omitted in the inset to expose base contact. Main assembled joint remains complete, no exploded unbound spear mistaken as functional. Minimal labels exactly "SUPPORTED BASE", "RESTRAINED SPLIT", "BINDING CLEAR OF EDGE", "ALIGNED AXIS". One small loose plant-target icon optional but no person, animal penetration, ballistic trajectory, atlatl, bow or arrow. Retain realistic thick wooden shaft, not polished factory pole.

Same lean adult about thirty, dark wavy ear-length hair, short beard, smooth ordinary skin. No indoor fire/smoke, no huge whole-front mud wall. Select one moment, not montage. No text, labels, watermark or logo.

Main focus inspectable joint rather than weapon brandishing.
